front.title: Restoration Evidence Records for AI Agent Incident Response

abstract.t: When an AI agent system is stopped, restricted or has its credentials revoked during an incident, someone later decides whether it may run again. Incident response guidance asks for that decision to be documented with the risk that remains, but no format says what the record must contain for a party outside the deploying organization to check it. This document defines five record types for that purpose: an incident action authorization, a revocation sweep, a re-enable decision, a joint authority assignment for incidents that span organizations, and a revocation boundary report. Each is an in-toto Statement carried in a DSSE envelope, uses the canonical form of the agent audit record, and is checked by ordered rules with a named reason for each failure. A bundle rule set binds a re-enable decision to the records it cites, by digest. A published conformance corpus carries a reject member for every rule that a member can force.
